items.title: Jack Lesberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

ctx.x: Milt Hinton credits you with a big break in his career. How did that come about?

He’s a great friend. Well I had the chance to recommend him. There was a period then when I was doing the Hit Parade and some of these other programs, that, when television started you know there was a lot of these commercials, like cigarette commercials of course. They didn’t like the idea of having blacks on their program, you know, coming from where the tobacco came from, and it was against their principles and so forth. So there was that kind of thing that was going on for a while. And also with Milt was the…
He was on the fast track.

items.title: Jack Lesberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well Milt then was one of the first black musicians to crack the market so to speak. [INTERVIEWEE] He was, yeah.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah, he was in with some hot — of course Bob Haggart is one of our, he was one of the first around those years too.
Well Milt then was one of the first black musicians to crack the market so to speak.
He was, yeah. And a couple of the guys from the Hit Parade finally put some on, I just can’t think of some of the names. I can see their faces but it just got by me for a minute.
